as_read: One 15 g/day RCT in post-infectious IBS-D is positive on a named primary; a meta-analysis of oral trials found no overall effect on gut permeability; sports trials are small with no named primary; N-acetyl-L-glutamine has no study read.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: intestinal permeability, no primary named in the abstract
studies_to_add.quote: Overall, glutamine supplementation did not significantly affect intestinal permeability (WMD: -0.00, 95% CI -0.04, 0.03).

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: not named; salivary IgA, nitric oxide, URTI incidence
studies_to_add.quote: Supplementation of L-glutamine significantly enhanced the concentrations of IgA and NO in saliva; additionally, the incidence of URTI was significantly reduced.

stored_rating_note: Stored positive_moderate on 30108163 reads right on the abstract's primary but is a single trial; the stored population fits. 32992440 is stored as neutral and is a tolerance study, not efficacy; the stored record's applicability text says so.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. Searches used: 2. The second combined glutamine reviews with N-acetyl-glutamine terms, returned 132, and printed the newest 30; among those, the N-acetyl hits were metabolomics, Mendelian randomization or preclinical, with no oral human trial, but this is not a complete N-acetyl search, so no rejection is proposed. A dedicated N-acetyl-L-glutamine search is owed before those 12 labels close. 41053591 (chemotherapy diarrhea meta-analysis), 38243579 (burn meta-analysis), 40748005 (pressure ulcers, with arginine) and the HMB/arginine/glutamine combination trials were listed by search but not opened; none is cited.
